mainTopic: Finishing רבי שמעון's view on carrying in a מבוי, then רבי יוחנן's limit on רבי אליעזר's rule that מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת
overview: This עמוד begins in the middle of a sentence. The גמרא is explaining why, according to רבי שמעון, one may carry in a certain מבוי. The first explanation is that a real מבוי needs both בתים and חצרות. That explanation is challenged, defended twice, and rejected twice. רב אשי then gives a new reason: the houses are what make the courtyards forbidden, and here the houses effectively drop out. A new topic follows. רבי יוחנן says that רבי אליעזר did not apply 'מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת' to every מצוה, since even שתי הלחם needed a גזירה שוה from the עומר. The גמרא shows that this גזירה שוה is מופנה on both sides. It then asks which מצוות are excluded. לולב, סוכה, מצה and שופר are all ruled out, and רב אדא בר אהבה answers: ציצית and מזוזה. רב יוסף explains that these have no fixed time, and אביי begins to challenge him. His challenge continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A real alleyway needs both houses and courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the מבוי is permitted. A מבוי requires houses and courtyards opening into it, and here there are houses but no courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: (A מבוי is defined as having) houses and courtyards opening into it. Here there are houses, but there are no courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud starts mid-sentence. The גמרא is finishing an explanation of why one may carry in this מבוי according to רבי שמעון: it lacks the full definition of a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By definition, a מבוי has courtyards opening into it, and each courtyard has houses. In this case the residents made an עירוב within each courtyard, so each courtyard merges with its houses into one unit. The result counts as 'houses' with no separate 'courtyards', so the strict rules of a מבוי do not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open into
Houses
Courtyards
There is / there is not

steps.confusionAlert: This amud opens mid-sentence. The start of the explanation ('a מבוי needs...') appears on the previous page.

phrases.english: houses and courtyards open into it,
phrases.notes: The end of the definition of a מבוי, begun on the previous page

phrases.english: and here, houses — there are,
courtyards — there are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun on the previous page
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מבוי lacks courtyards, so it does not meet the definition of a מבוי

steps.title: Then even without an עירוב, the alleyway should be missing houses
steps.stepSummary: If missing parts make a מבוי incomplete, then even when no עירוב was made, the houses should count as sealed. That would leave courtyards without houses, which is also incomplete.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even when they did not make an עירוב, let us view these houses as if they were sealed shut. Then there would be courtyards but no houses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation. By the same reasoning, the opposite case would also be permitted, and that is not what we hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, the residents may not carry from their houses into the courtyard. So the houses are useless for carrying and could be treated as walled off. That would leave 'courtyards with no houses', also short of a full מבוי. The explanation therefore proves too much.

keyTerms.meaning: They made an עירוב (joined their domains)
Let us view them
That are sealed / closed off

phrases.english: When they did not make an עירוב too,
let us view these houses
as though they were sealed,
so there are courtyards, and houses — there are not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would also exempt a מבוי where no עירוב was made, since its houses could be treated as sealed

steps.title: The houses can still be used by giving rights to one person
steps.stepSummary: Without an עירוב the houses are not truly 'sealed'. The residents can give up their rights to one person, and then carrying from that house is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible for all of them to give up their rights to one person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the first explanation. It shows that houses without an עירוב are not really out of the picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through ביטול רשות, all the residents can hand their rights to one resident. That resident may then carry between his house and the courtyard. So the houses still have potential use and cannot be called 'sealed'.

keyTerms.meaning: That they renounce (ביטול רשות)
Property rights / domain rights
To one person

phrases.english: It is possible for them to renounce
the rights of all of them to one person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: houses without an עירוב can still become usable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Houses without an עירוב are useless and can be treated as sealed
steps.terutzMaskana: Through ביטול רשות they can still be used, so they are not sealed

steps.title: That leaves only one house, not houses
steps.stepSummary: The defense fails. Giving rights to one person makes only a single usable house, but a מבוי needs multiple houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, there is one house, but there are not houses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rights can only be given to one person at a time, so only one house becomes usable. The definition requires 'בתים' in the plural, meaning at least two. So the challenge stands: the courtyards still lack houses.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end / ultimately
One house

phrases.english: Ultimately, one house there is,
houses there are not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 3
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It produces only one usable house, while the definition needs at least two

steps.title: Give the rights to two people at different times of day
steps.stepSummary: The residents can give their rights to one person for the morning and to another for the afternoon, producing two usable houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible: from morning until midday, to one person; from midday until evening, to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second defense to show that two houses can be in use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By splitting the day, two different houses each get a turn at being the usable house. That would supply the plural 'houses' that the definition requires.

keyTerms.meaning: From the morning
Midday
Toward evening

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר דְּמִצַּפְרָא וְעַד פַּלְגָא דְּיוֹמָא לְגַבֵּי חַד,
phrases.english: It is possible: from morning until midday, to one person,
from midday until evening, to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new defense against the rejection in step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one house can ever be usable
steps.terutzMaskana: Two houses can each be usable, one after the other

steps.title: At any moment only one house is usable
steps.stepSummary: This also fails. At any given time only one house has the rights, so there are never two houses at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, at the time this one has it, that one does not have it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the time-splitting answer, which collapses the whole first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the situation at a single moment. At every moment only one house is usable, so the plural requirement is never met. Since the defenses have failed, the challenge from step 2 stands, and the explanation from step 1 must be replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time
It is there / it is not there

phrases.english: Ultimately, at the time that this one has it,
that one does not have it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The time-splitting defense, and with it the whole 'houses and courtyards' explanation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There are never two usable houses at the same moment

steps.title: רב אשי: houses cause the prohibition, and here there are none
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new reason. Courtyards become forbidden only because of the houses. Once the houses are absorbed through the עירוב, nothing causes a prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: What caused the courtyards to be forbidden? The houses. And here there are none.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'אלא' signals that the old explanation is dropped. רב אשי explains the permit in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, courtyards and the מבוי count as one domain. The only thing that causes a prohibition is the houses, from which items might be carried out. Once the עירוב joins the houses to the courtyards, there are effectively no separate houses, so carrying in the מבוי is allowed. The question no longer depends on counting houses.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting what came before)
What caused
That they become forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: houses are the source of the prohibition. When the עירוב removes them from the picture, the מבוי becomes permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
What caused the courtyards to be forbidden?
The houses, and there are none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The permit depends on whether the מבוי meets the full definition
steps.terutzMaskana: The permit depends on the absence of houses, which are the cause of the prohibition
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once the houses merge with the courtyards, the cause of the prohibition is gone

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's rule does not apply to every מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that רבי אליעזר did not say 'מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת' as a rule for all מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי אליעזר did not say for every case that preparations for a מצוה override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי יוחנן limits how far רבי אליעזר's famous principle reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that preparations for a מצוה, such as making a knife for מילה, override שבת. רבי יוחנן says this is not an automatic rule for every מצוה. Each מצוה needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Preparations that make a מצוה possible
Override שבת
Not for everything

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying רבי אליעזר's rule is wrong. He is saying it is not a blanket rule for all מצוות.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not say for all cases
that preparations for a מצוה override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's rule of מכשירי מצוה is not universal

steps.title: Proof: even the two loaves needed a special derivation
steps.stepSummary: שתי הלחם are a fixed obligation of their day, yet רבי אליעזר learned that their preparations override שבת only through a גזירה שוה. So the rule is not automatic.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the two loaves are an obligation of the day, and רבי אליעזר learned them only from a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן proves his claim from how רבי אליעזר treats שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If preparations for every מצוה automatically overrode שבת, then שתי הלחם, an obligation fixed to that very day, would surely be included. Yet רבי אליעזר still needed a special גזירה שוה for them. This shows the rule has to be derived case by case.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves offered on שבועות
An obligation fixed to that day
A derivation from a shared word in two verses

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם חוֹבַת הַיּוֹם הֵן,
phrases.english: For the two loaves are an obligation of the day,
and Rabbi Eliezer did not learn them
except from a gezeirah shavah.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהֲרֵי שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם חוֹבַת הַיּוֹם הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement in step 8
steps.raayaObject: That מכשירי מצוה is not a universal rule for רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר needed a גזירה שוה even for שתי הלחם

steps.title: The ברייתא: the two loaves learned from the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר. The word 'הבאה' (bringing) appears both by the עומר and by שתי הלחם. Since the preparations for the עומר override שבת, so do the preparations for שתי הלחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says: From where do we know that the preparations for the two loaves override שבת? 'Bringing' is said by the עומר, and 'bringing' is said by the two loaves. Just as with the 'bringing' of the עומר the preparations override שבת, so too with the 'bringing' of the two loaves the preparations override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that proves רבי אליעזר needed a גזירה שוה for שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reaping of the עומר is allowed on שבת, so we know its preparations override שבת. The shared word 'הבאה' extends this to שתי הלחם. If a special source was needed here, the rule clearly is not automatic for every מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Bringing (the shared word)
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי אליעזר's rule needs a specific source for each מצוה. The proof is that even שתי הלחם required a גזירה שוה from the עומר.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From where do we know that the preparations for the two loaves
override Shabbat?
'Bringing' is stated regarding the omer,
and 'bringing' is stated regarding the two loaves.
Just as the 'bringing' stated regarding the omer —
its preparations override Shabbat,
so too the 'bringing' stated regarding the two loaves —
its preparations override Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cites the source for the claim in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר derived שתי הלחם only through a גזירה שוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the shared word 'הבאה' linking the עומר and שתי הלחם

steps.title: The matching words must be extra, or the comparison can be refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the גזירה שוה of 'הבאה' must be מופנה, meaning the words are extra in their verses. Otherwise one could point out a difference between the עומר and שתי הלחם and break the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words must be 'free' (extra). Because if they are not free, the comparison can be refuted: what is special about the עומר is that even if one found grain already cut, one must still cut fresh grain. Can you say the same about שתי הלחם, where if one found grain already cut, one does not need to cut more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to the גזירה שוה from Step 10. It says the shared word must be extra, and it shows the weakness we would face if it were not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה built on words that are not extra can be broken by pointing out a difference between the two cases. Here there is a real difference: the עומר must be freshly cut even if cut grain is available, but שתי הלחם can use grain that was already cut. Since the עומר is stricter about cutting, maybe only its preparations override שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Free' or extra. A word in a גזירה שוה that is not needed in its own verse, so it is available to teach something new.
'One can refute.' A logical difference can be found that breaks the comparison.
Grain that has already been cut.
He cuts (reaps) the grain.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the גזירה שוה here. It is only saying that the גזירה שוה works because the words are extra. The next step proves that they are.

phrases.english: They (the words) are free/extra.
phrases.notes: This is a condition placed on the גזירה שוה from Step 10.

phrases.english: For if they were not free,
one could refute it:
What about the עומר? It is special, because
if one found grain already cut, he still cuts fresh grain;
would you say the same of the two loaves,
where if one found grain already cut, he does not cut more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a requirement for the גזירה שוה brought in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of 'הבאה' only stands if the words are extra, because otherwise the difference in cutting rules would refute it.

steps.title: Proof that the word by the עומר is extra
steps.stepSummary: The verse already said 'וַהֲבֵאתֶם' about the עומר. So the later phrase 'מִיּוֹם הֲבִיאֲכֶם' is not needed in its own verse, and it is free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth, it is free. The verse already wrote 'You shall bring the עומר, the first of your harvest, to the כהן.' Why do I need 'from the day you brought'? Learn from this that it is extra, to be free for the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the 'bringing' word by the עומר is extra. The תורה already told us to bring the עומר, so repeating it shows the word is there to teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'מִיּוֹם הֲבִיאֲכֶם' adds nothing new about the עומר itself, it is available for the גזירה שוה. This answers the worry from Step 11, at least from the עומר side.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In truth' or 'indeed.' It introduces a defense.
'Since' or 'after all.' It introduces a verse that is already written.
'Why do I need it?' It points out an extra word or phrase.
'Learn from it.' It draws the conclusion.
'To make it free,' meaning available for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: In truth, it is indeed free:
Since it is already written:
'And you shall bring the sheaf (omer),
the first of your harvest, to the priest,'
why do I need 'from the day you brought'?
Learn from this that it is there to be free (for the comparison).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Meets the requirement set in Step 11 by showing the word is extra.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'הבאה' word by the עומר is free for a גזירה שוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repetition in ויקרא כג: 'וַהֲבֵאתֶם' (verse 10) and then 'מִיּוֹם הֲבִיאֲכֶם' (verse 15).

steps.title: Only one side is extra, and רבי אליעזר allows refuting that
steps.stepSummary: Only the עומר side has been shown to be extra. רבי אליעזר holds that a גזירה שוה that is extra on just one side can be learned from but can also be refuted. So the refutation from Step 11 comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, it is free from only one side. And we have heard that רבי אליעזר said that when it is free from one side, we learn from it but we can also refute it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 12. Proving the extra word on the עומר side alone is not enough for רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, a one-sided extra word still leaves the comparison open to refutation. So the difference about cutting grain could still break it. To be safe, the word must also be extra by שתי הלחם.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But still.' It shows a problem remains.
Free (extra) on only one side of the גזירה שוה.
We learn from it, but we may also refute it.

phrases.english: But still:
it is free from only one side,
and we have heard of רבי אליעזר
that he said: when it is free from one side,
we learn from it, but we can also refute it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 12 as not enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 12 that the גזירה שוה is safe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one side was shown to be extra, and רבי אליעזר allows refuting a one-sided גזירה שוה.

steps.title: The word is extra by שתי הלחם too
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תָּבִיאוּ' in the verse about שתי הלחם is also extra. So the גזירה שוה is free on both sides and cannot be refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall bring' is an extra inclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 13. It shows that the 'bringing' word is extra in the שתי הלחם verse as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תָּבִיאוּ' by שתי הלחם is not needed in its own context, so it counts as a ריבוי, an extra word. Now both sides are free. A two-sided free גזירה שוה cannot be refuted, so the difference in cutting rules no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall bring.' The word in the שתי הלחם verse.
An extra word or inclusion. Here it means the word is not needed in its place.

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה of 'הבאה' is extra on both sides, by the עומר and by שתי הלחם. So רבי אליעזר learns from it that the preparations for שתי הלחם override שבת, and the comparison cannot be refuted.

phrases.english: 'You shall bring' is an extra inclusion (so it is free on that side too).
phrases.notes: Refers to ויקרא כג:יז, about the two loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the second side of the comparison is also extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought only the עומר side was extra, which left the comparison open to refutation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides are free, so the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted.

steps.title: Which מצוות did רבי יוחנן mean to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement from Step 8. If רבי אליעזר did not say this rule for all מצוות, which מצוות are left out?
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's statement and asks a clarifying question. This sets up the next several attempts to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the rule מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת is not true for every מצוה. That implies some מצוות are excluded, and the גמרא wants to know which ones.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To exclude what?' It asks what a statement is meant to leave out.

phrases.english: To exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the גזירה שוה discussion and returns to רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצוות רבי יוחנן meant are not covered by מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Not לולב, since a ברייתא includes it
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that רבי יוחנן excludes לולב. This is rejected, because a ברייתא says that according to רבי אליעזר, לולב and all its preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it excludes לולב, but it was taught: לולב and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries לולב as the excluded מצוה and immediately rejects it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא openly says רבי אליעזר allows the preparations for לולב on שבת. So לולב cannot be what רבי יוחנן meant to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say.' It introduces a suggestion that will be tested.
The palm branch taken on סוכות.
Its preparations, the actions needed to make the מצוה possible.

phrases.english: If you say it is to exclude lulav,
but it was taught:
Lulav and all its preparations
override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First attempt to answer Step 15, which is rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects לולב as the excluded מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר allows the preparations for לולב on שבת.

steps.title: Not סוכה either
steps.stepSummary: The next suggestion is סוכה. It is rejected by a ברייתא saying that according to רבי אליעזר, סוכה and its preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes סוכה? But it was taught: סוכה and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, סוכה, and rejects it the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats. A ברייתא puts סוכה inside רבי אליעזר's rule, so it cannot be the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather.' It introduces a new suggestion after the last one failed.
The booth one lives in on סוכות.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude sukka?
But it was taught:
Sukka and all its preparations
override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second attempt, which is also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects סוכה as the excluded מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר allows the preparations for סוכה on שבת.

steps.title: Not מצה either
steps.stepSummary: The third suggestion is מצה. It is rejected because a ברייתא says that according to רבי אליעזר, מצה and its preparations override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes מצה? But it was taught: מצה and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries מצה and rejects it with another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like לולב and סוכה, the מצוה of מצה falls inside רבי אליעזר's rule, according to an explicit ברייתא. So it cannot be the exception רבי יוחנן meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Unleavened bread eaten on פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude matza?
But it was taught:
Matza and all its preparations
override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third attempt, which is also rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects מצה as the excluded מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר allows the preparations for מצה on שבת.

steps.title: Not שופר either
steps.stepSummary: The fourth suggestion is שופר. It is rejected by a ברייתא saying that according to רבי אליעזר, שופר and its preparations override שבת. The question from Step 15 still needs an answer, and Step 20 gives it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it excludes שופר? But it was taught: שופר and all its preparations override שבת. These are the words of רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries שופר, the last option, and rejects it too. This sets up the next step, where רב אדא בר אהבה gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every מצוה suggested so far is explicitly covered by רבי אליעזר in a ברייתא. So רבי יוחנן's exclusion must refer to some other מצוה. The next step names it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram's horn blown on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to exclude shofar?
But it was taught:
Shofar and all its preparations
override Shabbat;
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final attempt, which is rejected. The answer comes in Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects שופר as the excluded מצוה, which uses up the obvious options.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר allows the preparations for שופר on שבת.

steps.title: ציצית and מזוזה are excluded
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that רבי יוחנן meant to exclude attaching ציצית to a garment and putting a מזוזה on a doorway. Their preparations do not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: it is to exclude ציצית for one's garment and a מזוזה for one's doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the question from Step 15. The excluded מצוות are ציצית and מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה names the מצוות that fall outside רבי אליעזר's rule: attaching ציצית to a garment and putting up a מזוזה. Their preparations do not override שבת. He does not yet say why they are different. The גמרא asks that in step 22, and the first reason offered (רב יוסף's 'no fixed time') is immediately challenged by אביי in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: Fringes attached to a four-cornered garment.
His garment.
The scroll fixed to a doorpost.
His doorway.

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean ציצית and מזוזה are less important מצוות. The גמרא will ask in Step 22 why they are different, and the first answer offered there is disputed.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It is to exclude ritual fringes for his garment
and a mezuza for his doorway.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: לְמַעוֹטֵי צִיצִית לְטַלִּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer after all four suggestions failed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן meant ציצית and מזוזה, whose preparations do not override שבת even according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms: everyone agrees one is liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אדא בר אהבה. רבי אליעזר and the חכמים agree that someone who attaches ציצית or puts up a מזוזה on שבת is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: and they agree that if one attached ציצית to his garment or made a מזוזה for his doorway, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב אדא בר אהבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְשָׁוִין' (they agree) means even רבי אליעזר, who is usually lenient about preparations for a מצוה, agrees here. This confirms that ציצית and מזוזה are the exceptions רבי יוחנן had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way.' It introduces a ברייתא that supports a statement.
'And they agree.' Both sides of the argument agree here.
Liable, meaning he has violated שבת.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's rule, מכשירי מצוה דוחין את השבת, covers לולב, סוכה, מצה, שופר and שתי הלחם. It does not cover ציצית and מזוזה. For those, everyone agrees that doing them on שבת makes a person liable. The reason for this difference is debated in the steps that follow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit of רבי אליעזר's rule. The גמרא next asks what makes ציצית and מזוזה different, and the first answer offered, רב יוסף's, is challenged right away by אביי.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
And they agree that if one attached fringes to his garment
or made a mezuza for his doorway
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אדא בר אהבה's answer from Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת, even according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating 'וְשָׁוִין', that all agree one is liable.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone agrees that ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת. These are the מצוות רבי יוחנן meant to exclude.

steps.title: Why do ציצית and מזוזה not override שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אליעזר agrees that the preparations for ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question. Why does רבי אליעזר, who usually lets a מצוה's preparations override שבת, agree that ציצית and מזוזה are different?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that preparations for מילה, סוכה, מצה and שופר override שבת. So it is surprising that ציצית and מזוזה are an exception. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Fringes attached to a four-cornered garment
Parchment scroll fixed to a doorpost

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why does רבי אליעזר agree that the preparations for ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the agreement proven by the ברייתא in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ציצית and מזוזה are an exception to רבי אליעזר's general rule that a מצוה's preparations override שבת.

steps.title: These מצוות have no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that ציצית and מזוזה have no fixed time, so their preparations do not override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because they have no fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the reason. ציצית and מזוזה are not tied to a specific day, so there is no need to prepare them on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה must happen on day eight, and סוכה, מצה and שופר belong to set festival days. If those days fall on שבת, there is no other option. ציצית and מזוזה have no such deadline, so the preparation can be done before or after שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed time is set for them

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because they have no fixed time.
phrases.notes: They are not tied to a particular day, unlike מילה or the festival מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶם זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ציצית and מזוזה have no fixed time, so there is no need for their preparations to override שבת.

steps.title: אביי begins to turn רב יוסף's reason around
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to challenge רב יוסף. He says that the fact that these מצוות have no fixed time actually points the other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary, from the fact that they have no fixed time...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts objecting to רב יוסף's answer, but the sentence is not finished here. The גמרא is setting up the rest of his challenge, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אדרבה signals that אביי is flipping the logic. רב יוסף used 'no fixed time' to explain why these מצוות do not override שבת. אביי is about to argue that the same fact leads to the opposite conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
From the fact that...

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's sentence is cut off here. Do not decide what his conclusion is yet. The end of his argument comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, from the fact that they have no fixed time,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רב יוסף gave in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reason that ציצית and מזוזה do not override שבת because they have no fixed time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי turns the reason around, arguing that 'no fixed time' points to the opposite conclusion. The full argument continues on the next amud.
